column9: Speed is best defined as –
column14: the distance an object travels per unit of time
column15: how far an object has traveled in total
column16: the distance and direction from the starting point
column17: the time it takes an object to finish a trip
column28: Speed is the distance an object travels per unit of time (the rate of change of position), so S = d/t. Direction is not part of speed, and how far something went is distance, not speed.
column29: Think about the formula S = d/t. What is on top, and what is it divided by?

column9: Displacement is –
column14: how far an object has moved along its whole path
column15: the distance and direction from the starting point
column16: the speed of an object at one instant
column17: the total time an object is moving
column28: Displacement is the distance and direction from the starting point (the reference point). Distance is just how far something moved, with no direction.
column29: Which choice includes a direction and a starting point?

column9: The speed of an object at any given point of time, like the number on a speedometer, is called ___ speed.
column28: Instantaneous speed is the speed at any given point of time. Average speed is total distance ÷ total time for the whole trip.
column29: Think of what a speedometer shows at one moment.

column9: To find average speed for a trip with two parts, you should add the two speeds and divide by 2.
column28: False. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Averaging the speeds only works if the two parts take the same amount of time, so it is not the method to use.
column29: Look at the definition: average speed = total ___ ÷ total ___.

column9: Match each unit to the quantity it measures.
column28: Kilometers measure distance (how far), minutes measure time, and meters per second measure speed (distance per unit of time). A speed unit always has a distance unit divided by a time unit.
column29: A speed unit has a "per" in it: distance per time.

column9: Which of these are units of **speed**? Select all that apply.
column28: m/s, km/h, and mi/min are all a distance unit divided by a time unit, so they are speed units. Meters measures distance and hours measures time.
column29: A speed unit must be a distance unit divided by a time unit.

column9: Which formula is used to calculate speed?
column28: Speed = Distance/Time (S = d/t). Distance = speed × time and Time = Distance/Speed are the other two forms of the speed triangle.
column29: Speed is distance per unit of time. What does "per" tell you to do?

column9: Motion is movement or a change in position over time.
column28: True. Motion is movement or change in position over time. To tell that something moved, you compare its position to a reference point.
column29: If an object's position changes as time goes by, what is it doing?

column9: Riley runs 120 m across the football field in 15 s. What is her speed in m/s?
column28: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 120 m / 15 s. Answer: 8 m/s.
column29: Use S = d/t: distance on top, time on the bottom.

column9: Marcus walks to class at a constant speed of 3 m/s for 40 s. How far does he walk, in meters?
column28: Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 3 m/s × 40 s. Answer: 120 m (the seconds cancel).
column29: You know speed and time. Which form of the speed triangle gives distance?

column9: An object moving at a constant speed –
column16: covers more distance each second than the second before
column17: covers equal distances in equal amounts of time
column28: Constant speed means the speed does not change, so the object covers equal distances in equal amounts of time (for example, 5 m every second).
column29: Constant means it does not change. What stays the same each second?

column9: Distance is measured in ___ (m) in the metric system.
column28: Distance is how far something has moved, measured in meters (m). Larger distances can be in kilometers; in the U.S. we also use miles.
column29: It is the SI base unit of length.

column9: Which of these is an example of **changing** speed?
column14: a car pulling away from a stop sign
column15: a car on cruise control at 55 mph on a straight road
column17: a conveyor belt moving 0.5 m/s all day
column28: A car pulling away from a stop sign is speeding up, so its speed is changing. The other choices keep the same speed the whole time.
column29: Which object's speedometer reading would go up or down?

column9: Distance and displacement are always the same number for any trip.
column28: False. Distance is how far you moved along the whole path; displacement is the distance and direction from the starting point. If you turn around, distance keeps adding up but displacement gets smaller.
column29: What happens to your displacement if you walk away from home and then walk back?

column9: In the speed triangle, **d** is on top and **s** and **t** are on the bottom. If you cover up **d**, what is left?
column28: Covering d leaves s and t side by side, which means multiply: d = s × t. Covering s leaves d over t (S = d/t), and covering t leaves d over s (t = d/s).
column29: Side by side in the triangle means multiply; one over the other means divide.

column9: Andrea bikes 27.6 km on a trail in 2.4 hours. What is her average speed in km/h?
column28: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 27.6 km / 2.4 h. Answer: 11.5 km/h.
column29: Distance goes on top, time on the bottom. Units: km over h.

column9: Raegan swims at an average speed of 1.6 m/s. How many seconds will it take her to finish a 100 m race?
column28: Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 100 m / 1.6 m/s. Answer: 62.5 s. A common mistake is multiplying 100 × 1.6.
column29: You know distance and speed. In the triangle, cover t: what is left?

column9: Marcus drives on Highway 29 at 62 mph for 2.5 hours. How many miles does he travel?
column28: Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 62 mi/h × 2.5 h. Answer: 155 miles (hours cancel).
column29: Speed × time = distance. Check that the time is already in hours.

column9: A tarantula crawls 3.6 m across the lab floor in 8 s. What is its speed in m/s?
column28: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 3.6 m / 8 s. Answer: 0.45 m/s. Dividing 8 by 3.6 is the common mistake.
column29: Distance on top. Your answer should be less than 1 m/s for a spider.

column9: A horse gallops at 13.5 m/s. How many seconds does it take to cover 810 m?
column28: Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 810 m / 13.5 m/s. Answer: 60 s.
column29: Time = Distance / Speed.

column9: Liv walks to class at 1.4 m/s. It takes her 95 s to get there. How many meters does she walk?
column28: Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 1.4 m/s × 95 s. Answer: 133 m.
column29: Which form of the triangle has s and t side by side?

column9: Bradley runs 2.4 miles in 20 minutes. What is his speed in miles per minute (mi/min)?
column28: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 2.4 mi / 20 min. Answer: 0.12 mi/min. The answer unit is mi/min, so no conversion to hours is needed.
column29: The answer unit is mi/min, so keep the time in minutes.

column9: A group of bikers take a 3-hour trip. In the first 2 hours they ride 46 km, and in the last hour they ride 17 km. What is their average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
column28: Formula: average speed = total distance / total time. Set Up: (46 km + 17 km) / 3 h = 63 km / 3 h. Answer: 21 km/h.
column29: Add up all the distance first, then divide by the total time.

column9: Jae walks 300 m in 240 s, then runs 500 m in 160 s. What is his average speed for the whole trip, in m/s?
column28: Formula: average speed = total distance / total time. Set Up: (300 m + 500 m) / (240 s + 160 s) = 800 m / 400 s. Answer: 2 m/s.
column29: Total distance ÷ total time. Do not find two speeds and average them.

column9: Liv divides a distance in kilometers by a time in hours. What unit should her answer have?
column28: Speed units come straight from S = d/t: km divided by h gives km/h. Multiplying would give km·h, which is not a speed unit.
column29: Write the units as a fraction just like the numbers: distance unit over time unit.

column9: A horse runs at 12 m/s for 30 s. Which setup finds how far the horse runs?
column28: You know speed and time, so use d = s × t: 12 m/s × 30 s = 360 m. Dividing would give a unit that is not a distance.
column29: Cover d in the speed triangle. Are s and t side by side or stacked?

column9: Marcus walks 120 m east down Main Street, then turns around and walks 45 m west. How far is he from his starting point, in meters? (His displacement is east; give the number only.)
column28: Displacement is the distance and direction from the starting point. Opposite directions subtract: 120 m − 45 m = 75 m east. Adding them (165 m) gives the distance, not the displacement.
column29: He walked back toward the start. Should you add or subtract?

column9: Andrea jogs 80 m north, then turns around and jogs 35 m south. What total **distance** did she travel, in meters?
column28: Distance is how far she moved along her whole path, with no direction: 80 m + 35 m = 115 m. Subtracting gives her displacement (45 m north), not her distance.
column29: Distance counts every meter she moved, no matter the direction.

column9: A runner who finishes one full lap back at the starting line has a displacement of zero, even though her distance is not zero.
column28: True. Displacement is distance and direction from the starting point. Ending where you started means zero displacement, but the distance is the full length of the lap.
column29: Where does the runner end up compared to where she started?

column9: The number on a car's speedometer shows the car's –
column28: A speedometer shows the speed at that moment: the instantaneous speed. Average speed would need the total distance and total time of the trip.
column29: Does a speedometer show the whole trip or just right now?

column9: Put the steps for solving a speed problem in order.
column14: Substitute the numbers with their units into the formula
column15: Write the answer with the correct units
column16: Write the formula from the speed triangle
column28: Write the Formula first, then the Set Up (put the numbers with units in), then calculate, and finish with the Answer with units.
column29: Mr. Erickson's format: Formula / Set Up / Answer with units.

column9: A football player sprints 36.6 m in 4.0 s. What is his average speed in m/s?
column28: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 36.6 m / 4.0 s. Answer: 9.15 m/s.
column29: Distance on top, time on the bottom.

column9: Liv's family drives 175 km at an average speed of 70 km/h. How many hours does the drive take?
column28: Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 175 km / 70 km/h. Answer: 2.5 h (km cancel and hours are left).
column29: Time = Distance / Speed. Which unit cancels?

column9: Which of these describe an object moving at a **constant** speed? Select all that apply.
column14: Its speedometer reading stays the same.
column17: Its instantaneous speed always equals its average speed.
column18: It stops at every stop sign.
column28: At constant speed the speedometer reading stays the same, the object covers the same distance every second, and its instantaneous speed equals its average speed. Speeding up downhill or stopping at stop signs means changing speed.
column29: Constant speed means the speed never changes during the trip.

column9: Bradley rides his scooter at 18 km/h for 0.75 hours. How many kilometers does he travel?
column28: Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 18 km/h × 0.75 h. Answer: 13.5 km.
column29: Speed × time = distance. The time is already in hours.

column9: Raegan drives 12 miles in 15 minutes, then 30 miles in 45 minutes. What is her average speed for the whole trip, in mph? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Formula: average speed = total distance / total time. Set Up: total d = 12 + 30 = 42 mi; total t = 15 + 45 = 60 min = 1 h. S = 42 mi / 1 h. Answer: 42 mph.
column29: Find total distance and total time, then change the minutes to hours before dividing.

column9: Marcus bikes 30 km at 15 km/h, then bikes another 30 km at 30 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole 60 km trip, in km/h?
column28: First find each time: t = d/s, 30/15 = 2 h and 30/30 = 1 h. Average speed = total distance / total time = 60 km / 3 h = 20 km/h. Averaging the speeds (22.5 km/h) is wrong because he spent more time going slow.
column29: You can't average the two speeds. Use t = d/s to find the time for each part first.

column9: Liv runs 400 m at 4 m/s, then 400 m at 8 m/s. She says her average speed is 6 m/s because (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6. Which statement is correct?
column14: She is right; the average of the two speeds is always the average speed.
column15: She is wrong; it is about 5.33 m/s because she spent more time going slower.
column16: She is wrong; it is 12 m/s because you add the speeds.
column17: She is wrong; it is about 6.67 m/s because she spent more time going faster.
column28: Her times are 400/4 = 100 s and 400/8 = 50 s, so average speed = 800 m / 150 s = 5.33 m/s. She spent more time at the slower speed, so the average is below 6 m/s.
column29: Find the time for each part with t = d/s, then use total distance ÷ total time.

column9: Andrea drives 9 miles across Cadott in 12 minutes. What is her speed in miles per hour (mph)? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Change minutes to hours: 12 min ÷ 60 = 0.2 h. Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 9 mi / 0.2 h. Answer: 45 mph. Dividing by 12 gives mi/min (0.75), not mph.
column29: The answer must be in miles per HOUR. Convert 12 minutes to hours first.

column9: A runner covers 3.6 km in 12 minutes. What is the runner's speed in m/s? (1 km = 1000 m; 1 minute = 60 s)
column28: Convert: 3.6 km × 1000 = 3600 m and 12 min × 60 = 720 s. Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 3600 m / 720 s. Answer: 5 m/s.
column29: Convert both values first: km to m and minutes to seconds. Then use S = d/t.

column9: Bradley drives 18 miles at 54 mph. How many **minutes** does the trip take? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 18 mi / 54 mi/h = 0.333 h. Convert: 0.333 h × 60 = 20 min.
column29: Use t = d/s to get hours first, then multiply by 60 to get minutes.

column9: Riley drives on Highway 29 at 64 mph for 45 minutes. How many miles does she travel? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Convert: 45 min ÷ 60 = 0.75 h. Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 64 mi/h × 0.75 h. Answer: 48 miles. Multiplying 64 × 45 is the minutes-vs-hours mistake.
column29: The speed is per HOUR, so the time must be in hours before you multiply.

column9: Jae walks 30 m east, then 40 m north. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line (the size of his displacement), in meters? (Use a^{2} + b^{2} = c^{2}.)
column28: The two legs make a right angle, so c = √(30^{2} + 40^{2}) = √2500 = 50 m. His distance walked is 70 m, but his displacement is only 50 m (northeast).
column29: Draw the path. The straight line back to the start is the long side of a right triangle.

column9: A jogger runs 600 m north, then turns around and runs 200 m south. The whole run takes 400 s. What is the jogger's average speed, in m/s?
column28: Average speed uses total distance, not displacement: (600 m + 200 m) / 400 s = 800 m / 400 s = 2 m/s. Using the displacement (400 m) gives 1 m/s, which is the wrong quantity.
column29: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Does distance care about direction?

column9: A tarantula crawls at 0.04 m/s for 3 minutes. How many meters does it crawl? (1 minute = 60 s)
column28: Convert: 3 min × 60 = 180 s. Formula: d = s × t. Set Up: d = 0.04 m/s × 180 s. Answer: 7.2 m.
column29: The speed is per SECOND, so change the minutes to seconds first.

column9: Which trip has the greatest average speed? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Convert minutes to hours and use S = d/t: 120 km / 2 h = 60 km/h; 200 km / 4 h = 50 km/h; 45 km / 0.5 h = 90 km/h; 15 km / 0.25 h = 60 km/h. The 45 km trip is fastest even though it is short.
column29: Put every trip in km/h first. 30 minutes is what part of an hour?

column9: A car travels at 25 m/s. How many seconds does it take to travel 1.5 km? (1 km = 1000 m)
column28: Convert: 1.5 km × 1000 = 1500 m. Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 1500 m / 25 m/s. Answer: 60 s.
column29: Speed is in meters per second, so change km to m before dividing.

column9: Liv bikes 4 km in 10 minutes, rests for 5 minutes, then bikes 6 km in 15 minutes. What is her average speed for the whole trip, including the rest, in km/h? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
column28: Total distance = 4 + 6 = 10 km. Total time = 10 + 5 + 15 = 30 min = 0.5 h (the rest counts). Average speed = 10 km / 0.5 h = 20 km/h.
column29: Average speed uses the total time from start to finish, including stops. Convert minutes to hours.

column9: Rank these speeds from **slowest** to **fastest**. (1 km = 1000 m; 1 minute = 60 s; 1 hour = 3600 s)
column28: Change all to m/s: tarantula 0.5 m/s; walker 5000 m / 3600 s ≈ 1.39 m/s; cyclist 300 m / 60 s = 5 m/s; horse 900 m / 60 s = 15 m/s.
column29: You can only compare speeds in the same unit. Convert each one to m/s.

column9: Raegan swims 200 m at 1.25 m/s. Jae finds her time by doing 200 × 1.25 = 250 s. What did Jae do wrong?
column17: He should have divided 200 by 1.25 because t = d/s.
column28: To find time you use t = d/s: 200 m / 1.25 m/s = 160 s. Jae multiplied, which is the form for distance (d = s × t), and his units would come out m²/s, not s.
column29: Cover t in the speed triangle. Is d over s, or side by side with s?
